bug.title: Owned Gateway external exit lacks bounded identity-safe recovery
bug.summary: GitHub issue 12 reports that Gateway disappearance is presented as a misleading permission failure. The core repair requires accurate failure state and at most one identity- and generation-bound recovery attempt.

basis: current-target source red not established yet

reproduction.state: historical-observed; isolated owned-child kill fixture pending
steps: Start a fake owned Gateway using temporary state, fake secrets, and a dynamic loopback port.
Kill only that exact owned child and observe the Desktop runtime state transition.
Permit one restart only when config generation, executable identity, ownership record, and path-secret identity are unchanged.
Inject generation drift, identity drift, and a second exit; assert no retry loop and no profile, journal, or secret drift.
reproduction.observed: Issue 12 reports a generic 403 or permission-style symptom after the proxy process exits instead of an accurate Gateway failure and recovery path.

confirmed_facts.statement: GitHub issue 12 remains open and describes Gateway external exit with misleading user-visible failure.

hypotheses.statement: The current runtime owner may not supervise the Gateway child after initial startup.
